ideas.title: Narrative is the recurrent locus of editorial hierarchy drift — make Narrative the primary control point for company‑first framing
ideas.description: Across experiments 007–009 the Narrative stage is the most common first-visible place where a company-first editorial hierarchy breaks and unsupported claims are introduced. Prioritizing a Narrative-focused gate or intervention offers the strongest, evidence-backed opportunity to prevent downstream reframing toward product/technical-first stories.
ideas.audience: Internal content/experiment teams, prompt engineers, editorial leads working on Nuëyon.Compose pipeline orchestration and quality control.
ideas.rationale: Why it matters: The report documents Narrative as the first observable hierarchy shift in many runs (007 runs 001–002; 008 A-002; 009 baseline 002/003 and candidates 001–003). Because Narrative directly crafts the reader-facing through-line, targeting it can block recurring downstream amplifications in Compose. Gaps and uncertainty: Narrative is not the sole origin — some runs show Idea or Synthesis as the first drift (e.g., 007 candidate 003, 008 Idea-origin runs), so a Narrative-only fix may not eliminate all failures. A controlled test is required to confirm impact and to avoid missing upstream causes.
ideas.evidence: Explicit statements in the report: “Narrative is the most recurrent first visible hierarchy shift in the available records.” Localized examples: Experiment 007 — Narrative first in candidate 001–002; Experiment 008 A-002 — Narrative invents founders and product leads; Experiment 009 — Narrative is the first clear editorial shift in baseline 002 and 003 and in candidate 001–003. The report also notes that Narrative failures then persist into Compose in multiple runs.

ideas.title: Narrative is the recurrent locus of pipeline drift — run a controlled upstream-boundary trial focused on Narrative
ideas.description: Across Experiments 007–009 the Narrative stage is the most frequent first point where a company-first introduction shifts into a product- or orchestration-led story or where unsupported audience/validation claims appear. The strongest editorial opportunity is a focused trial that treats Narrative as the tested decision boundary: preserve the selected company-level subject and product-as-support relationship through story selection, then measure whether that prevents downstream hierarchy and claim inflation.
ideas.audience: Internal content/product teams, prompt and workflow engineers, experiment designers responsible for Nuëyon.Compose editorial integrity.
ideas.rationale: The source provides repeated, concrete examples where Narrative either initiates or clearly amplifies hierarchy breaks and factual overclaims; a controlled trial targeted at Narrative is the lowest-assumption way to test remediation. This idea matters because it focuses scarce experimentation capacity on the stage most often implicated by the evidence, increasing the chance of a clear, diagnostic result that distinguishes whether the problem is Narrative framing (vs Idea, Synthesis, or Compose). It is supported by the report’s recommendation to run a single controlled upstream-boundary trial and by the per-run localization tables. Gaps/uncertainty: causation is not established — Narrative’s role may be upstream-influenced in some runs (Synthesis/Idea sometimes start the drift), so the trial must preserve identical upstream inputs to isolate Narrative’s effect.
ideas.evidence: Experiment 007: Narrative is first visible drift in candidate runs 001–002; candidate 003 shifts at Synthesis but Narrative inherits the break. Experiment 008: A-002’s first factual breach occurs at Narrative; multiple A runs show Narrative making orchestration-centered framing explicit. Experiment 009: Narrative is the first clear hierarchy shift in baseline 002/003 and in candidates 001–003; several examples in the report show Narrative inventing unsupported audiences or elevating orchestration to company direction. The report’s “Implication for the next focused trial” explicitly recommends targeting Narrative as the most recurrent locus and preserving company-first subject through story selection.

ideas.title: Find where the story first changes before choosing what to fix
ideas.description: Use the saved pipeline examples to show why the next controlled trial should target the earliest stage supported by the evidence for the chosen failure. Where Narrative appears to be the first shift, inspect the actual Synthesis it received before changing Narrative.
ideas.audience: People investigating editorial drift in the Nuëyon.Compose pipeline
ideas.rationale: The same company-first story can change at different points. Localizing the selected failure first gives the team a way to choose one focused trial while keeping observation and causation separate.
ideas.evidence: The report locates the first visible hierarchy break in Narrative in 007 candidates 001–002 and in Synthesis in candidate 003. Some 008 company-first runs change at Idea. The next-trial recommendation says to target the first evidence-supported stage for the chosen failure and compare Narrative with its actual Synthesis input before changing it.

blockingIssues.constraint: Intervention selection depends on the earliest supported deviation in the chosen case. Recurrence establishes neither cause nor preventive effect.
blockingIssues.sourceEvidence: Cross-experiment patterns and Implication for the next focused trial describe varying first drift across Idea, Synthesis and Narrative and inspecting actual Synthesis before changing Narrative.
blockingIssues.problem: Narrative is made the primary intervention and prevention is claimed from recurrence.

blockingIssues.constraint: The source leaves the intervention stage conditional on case evidence, including possible upstream drift.
blockingIssues.sourceEvidence: Implication for the next focused trial conditions intervention on the chosen failure and upstream evidence.
blockingIssues.problem: The proposed controlled trial still fixes Narrative as the decision boundary in advance.
